data.turoyo: <...> Kulle mbawašše, kṯəwwe w əzzənwo l rišayye w šəqliwole. <...>
data.translation: <...> They had assessed all of them, written them down, and they would go to them and take it. <...>

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; a complete assessment-to-collection sequence clarifies levy collection without inventing a tax-specific sense. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: Jan Beṯ-Şawoce: the supplied English is project machine translation. All semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo; English quotations are retained verbatim and are not edition translations.
The Turoyo sequence assessment/registration, going to contributors, then taking the payment supports a levy rather than a light-verb idiom. The money amount is implicit.
This institutional coercion context broadens the inherited village-contribution examples but does not by itself require a new sense. No round 1 job exists.
Does kulle in Jan 2.4/1116 index taxpayers or all assessed amounts, and does mbawašše mean assessing a share specifically or imposing the levy more generally?
The levy can be assessed against all taxpayers before collection; the human/collective object kulle contrasts with the inherited five-paper-pound amount and ʕal contributor.
